_comment: The scenery registry: everything visible that is NOT a gameplay tile. A redwood trunk 400 pixels tall, a foreground branch cropped by the frame, a silhouetted ridge in the far distance. Tiles are the world the player walks on; scenery is the world they look at. scripts/scenery_registry.gd reads this, scripts/scene_planes.gd places it, maps reference it by name in a "scenery" array.
_anchor: The one number that matters, exactly as it is for a tile or a pack: the pixel INSIDE the image that touches the ground. It is placed at the cell's ground position and it is what the prop sorts by. A 400px redwood and a 48px villager standing on the same cell sort identically, because both are sorted by their feet and neither by their picture.
_planes: "plane" is the default depth plane a prop belongs in -- far_background, playable, foreground, screen_background, screen_foreground. A placement may override it. Only the playable plane is y-sorted; the others are ordered by their "sort" key. See docs/architecture/scenery.md.
_materials: "normal" and "emission" name layout-identical sibling images by the same convention packs and tile atlases use. Optional, and dormant until a source ships them.
_empty: There is no production scenery yet, on purpose: this migration builds the contract, not the forest. A prop added here needs no engine change -- registry entry, map placement, done.
